name: United Kingdom

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. United Kingdom mid-2025 population estimate of the Office for National Statistics, 69 487 000 inhabitants, published 27 November 2025, read on the ONS population estimates page. Eurostat was deliberately not used here: its demo_pjan series stops at 1 January 2020 for the United Kingdom, a consequence of the country leaving the Union, and a five-year-old figure was refused when the national statistical institute publishes a current one. Note the reference differs from the rest of the series: ONS gives a mid-year estimate, Eurostat a 1 January stock. The gap is a few months of growth and is not material at the precision this indicator uses, but it is recorded rather than hidden.

Collected on 2026-07-28, in English, in the transversal venues pass. Three units, three houses, against an opening estimate of 5 produced with no research. The candidate list is unusually clean for once: the British Puppet Guild keeps a register of UK puppet theatres and seven of them hold a building. All seven were then read one at a time, and the split between the three that count and the four that do not is almost entirely a split on public money rather than on puppetry. The Little Angel Theatre has stood in Dagmar Passage in Islington since 1961, calls itself the home of British puppetry, and is one of only three building-based puppet theatres in England; a hundred seats with the workshop beside them where the puppets are carved, and Arts Council England behind it. The Norwich Puppet Theatre occupies the medieval church of St James the Less at Whitefriars, Grade I listed, has made work for more than forty years, and carries annual core funding of 7 250 pounds from Norwich City Council beside Arts Council project grants of 28 908 pounds for the year to 31 March 2024. The Scottish Mask & Puppet Centre at 8-10 Balcarres Avenue in Kelvindale is Scotland's primary venue and resource centre for mask, puppet, magic, mime and physical theatre, and is core-funded through Glasgow Life by Glasgow City Council. Its site redevelopment was still under way at the time of reading and that is recorded rather than smoothed over: the core funding is the fact that counts it, not the state of the building. The four refused are the reason this country is worth writing up. Every one of them has a hall and none has public backing. The Puppet Theatre Barge at Little Venice is a seventy-two-foot Thames lighter that the Movingstage Marionettes converted into a permanent marionette theatre with a stage built for string puppets, wintering in London and going up the river in summer since 1986. Biggar Puppet Theatre in Lanarkshire is a miniature Victorian theatre of a hundred seats built for the Purves Puppets in 1987, and its own appeal states the position exactly: it is not a charity with any regular funding and lives on ticket sales. Upfront Puppet Theatre in Eden is purpose-built. The Harlequin Puppet Theatre at Rhos-on-Sea is the oldest of them all, built by Eric Bramall in 1958 as the first purpose-built puppet theatre in Great Britain, closed after its operator died in 2023, listed Grade II to secure the building, and reopening under new management with two performances in December 2025 and wider plans for 2026 pending a licence. Heritage protection is a public act about a building and not support to a puppetry unit, so it does not count as backing. Three is therefore a statement about the British funding settlement, in which puppetry houses subsist on the box office, and not about British puppetry. The upper bound is set at 7 because all four refusals turn on one unread or absent fact each, and any of them could move.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. No establishment retained, on a recent and documented closure. The Royal Central School of Speech and Drama, part of the University of London, carried the United Kingdom's first university puppetry award, the BA in Puppetry: Design and Performance, the country's only puppetry BA and a pillar of the school's training for more than twenty-five years. That course has taken no new students since the 2018-19 academic year and is no longer taught; puppetry survives as a component embedded in other courses, from Theatre Practice to Acting and Applied Theatre. A puppetry master's is announced as in development, with no source establishing that it has opened. As things stand no training satisfies the denominator and the value moves from 0.5 to 0. Upper bound at 1 to carry that announced master's: if its opening is confirmed, the United Kingdom returns to 1. Estimate, the school's site refusing automated reading.
